name: Individual Genesis creditor (4,064 BTC)
technique: Staged phishing (voice, email, screen sharing); Remote desktop/social engineering
classificationNote: Classified by TypeSafe jev-1.13.0 (confidence 0.92). Replaced keyword guess "key-compromise".
rootCause: On August 19, 2024, attackers stole 4,064 BTC (worth about $243M) from an individual creditor of Genesis using staged phishing and remote desktop access. The thieves impersonated Google and Gemini support for account access, then extracted private keys during a screen-sharing session. Law enforcement froze $9M and returned $500K, with most funds unrecovered. Staged social engineering targeting off-chain account credentials and document records. Attackers manipulated the victim into installing remote desktop software, opened files with BTC private keys over a shared screen, and swept all holdings. No protocol or wallet software vulnerability involved.
